subject: Day 45: introduce a lights-out song
bodyText:
Today's focus
Day 45, the back half of week seven. Crying is tapering and night stretches are inching toward 4-5 hours for some infants, which makes this the right week to install a single repeatable sleep-onset cue before the 2-month visit reshuffles the routine.

Action items
- Pick one lights-out song and sing it at the same point every night, after the bath and before the crib, so the pairing becomes the cue rather than the song itself. Circadian rhythm is still consolidating at six to 12 weeks, so a consistent association does more than any schedule right now. AAP HealthyChildren on getting your baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Keep the sleep space compliant as you build the routine: Avi on his back every sleep, alone in the bassinet or crib, firm flat mattress, no loose bedding, room at 68-72F. AAP HealthyChildren on infant sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/default.aspx
- Confirm the 2-month well visit is on the calendar within the next one to two weeks and start a feeding and output log to bring.

Watch-fors
- [low concern] Drool starting; this is early salivary-gland maturation, not necessarily teething, since first teeth usually arrive at six to 10 months.
- [low concern] Rolling-eye episodes as he drifts off during sleep transitions.
- [monitor] Persistent head tilt to one side with limited rotation, which can be torticollis from in-utero positioning; flag it for a physical-therapy referral at the 2-month visit.
- [call within 24h] Persistent vomiting beyond 24 hours, or refusal of multiple feeds in a row.
- [call now] Rectal temperature at or above 100.4F (38.0C), lethargy, refusing all feeds, blue or grey color, or labored breathing. Call 911 for blue lips!

Enrichment opportunities
- Sing the same lights-out song every night just before the crib to start building a durable sleep-onset association; the predictability is the active ingredient. AAP HealthyChildren on getting your baby to sleep: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Getting-Your-Baby-to-Sleep.aspx
- Stagger 30-45 minutes of tummy time across short bouts and prompt forearm push-ups, which build the neck and shoulder strength that precedes rolling and sitting. AAP HealthyChildren on tummy time: https://www.healthychildren.org/English/ages-stages/baby/sleep/Pages/Back-to-Sleep-Tummy-to-Play.aspx
- Smile and talk to him face-to-face during awake-alert windows and watch for the responsive smile back, the hallmark social milestone of this window. AAP Bright Futures: https://www.aap.org/en/practice-management/bright-futures/bright-futures-tools-and-resources/

Upcoming
- Day 49: crying typically tapering noticeably; 2-month visit prep week.
- Day 56-70: 2-month well visit and first vaccines (HepB #2, RV #1, DTaP #1, Hib #1, PCV #1, IPV #1).
- Day 57-72: post-vaccine 24-48 hour window of fussiness and low-grade fever.

Developmental milestone check-in
Tap any link to mark it complete. View or change others at https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones

- Looks at a toy for several seconds
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained visual attention — precedes reaching.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/looks-at-toy-several-seconds/complete

- Coos or makes sounds beyond crying
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Vowel sounds like ooh, ahh. Pre-language vocalization. Distinct from fussing or hiccup sounds.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/coos-makes-sounds/complete

- Holds head up while on tummy
  AAP window: day 35-60
  What to look for: Sustained head lift of several seconds, not just a brief bob. Forearms may or may not be supporting yet.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/holds-head-up-tummy/complete

- Hands relax open most of the time
  AAP window: day 35-90
  What to look for: Newborn fists relax as the palmar grasp reflex fades. Predictor of voluntary grasp coming.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/hands-open-mostly/complete

- First social smile (responding to a face, not gas)
  AAP window: day 28-60
  What to look for: Smile in response to someone smiling or talking to them, not a reflexive gas smile. Hallmark social milestone.
  Source: https://www.cdc.gov/act-early/milestones/2-months.html
  Mark complete: https://www.noahhshaw.com/baby/milestones/first-social-smile/complete
